description:
GENERATED — do not edit. Regenerate with `python scripts/build_specs.py`.

Every SURVIVOR and CACHE row of `promptpotter/infrastructure/store/data_root.py`, by its patterns
under the data root: a diff in a SURVIVOR's shape owes a migration
(`promptpotter/application/maintenance/migrate.py::MIGRATIONS`) the landing runs before the code
that reads it does; a CACHE file that stops loading is dropped by the landing, which says so.

shape.description: A configuration as its archive file holds it: nothing any dataset or answer says of it.
shape.title: ArchiveConfig

NodeKind.description: Closed: an unlisted ``type:`` is refused at parse. A GATEWAY runs another pipeline and owns no config.
NodeKind.title: NodeKind

OptimizerPromptTemplate.description: A prompt the optimizer RUNS ON (`dispatch/llm_call`), never one it produces.
OptimizerPromptTemplate.title: OptimizerPromptTemplate

shape.description: The bench's check-in `pipeline.yaml`: one llm node, `checkin`, whose config holds no knob.
shape.title: CheckinPipelineManifest

PrincipalGrant.description: An empty ``delegated_by`` is a DENIED grant: own tenant, no command caps, never an owner.
PrincipalGrant.title: PrincipalGrant

Presumption.description: What a block's text takes for granted of the run it lands in; a run lacking one makes it noise.
Presumption.title: Presumption

PromptPart.description: A prompt field a snippet suits, one name for a target and an optimizer prompt alike: a drop elsewhere is shown, never refused.
PromptPart.title: PromptPart

CampaignLaunch.description: A campaign run: its hop is UNRESOLVED until a fresh mint names the cycle.
CampaignLaunch.title: CampaignLaunch

EmbeddedRun.description: A host program's run: a share and a reservation, never a slot, since the host schedules itself.
EmbeddedRun.title: EmbeddedRun

InnerRun.description: An L4 inner campaign: a share of what its enclosing run's book has left, and nothing more.
InnerRun.title: InnerRun

PaidCall.description: One LLM call outside any run (a check-in, a chat turn): a hold, never a slot.
PaidCall.title: PaidCall

Refusal.description: A refusal as served: the rest of the answer it rides in serves on beside it.

code.description: The code a client branches on: the refusal's kind.
code.title: Code

message.description: The sentence an operator reads, naming its remedy and the Account tab it lives in, where it names one.
message.title: Message

Refusal.title: Refusal

ScoringPass.description: A paid verb scoring outside any run: its hop is the cycle it scores, or none at all.
ScoringPass.title: ScoringPass

StopReason.description: Why a cycle's run ended or paused.
StopReason.title: StopReason

shape.description: Outlives its release to the end of its UTC day: the daily launch quota counts it.
shape.title: Job

TokenAccount.description:
What ONE metered thing consumed: a provider round-trip, a measured row or a searchpoint.

``reasoning`` is a subset of ``output`` and both cache counts of ``input``, never further
totals. A null ``cache_read`` means no breakdown was reported; ``0`` means one was, with no hit.
TokenAccount.title: TokenAccount

ToolCall.description: One call a model asked for: ``arguments`` parsed, never the wire's JSON string.
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

cost_usd.description: What the PROVIDER says the call cost, summed across a repair retry (both round-trips are billed). Its own field rather than a ``usage`` key because ``usage`` counts tokens and this is money. ``None`` means the provider reported nothing — the honest answer, never a zero nobody measured. The call is then priced at our rate in its own field (``telemetry.py::rate_priced_usd``), never in this one.
cost_usd.title: Cost Usd

finish_reason.description: Why the provider stopped the FINAL attempt, in the OpenAI spelling every client normalizes to — ``length`` is a ``max_tokens`` hit. An earlier attempt's own reason leads its ``schema_repair_errors`` entry. ``None`` where the provider reported none.
finish_reason.title: Finish Reason

parsed.description: Parsed response. Typed Pydantic instance when ``chat`` was called with ``response_model``; plain dict when only ``response_schema`` was supplied; ``None`` for text-mode.
parsed.title: Parsed

reasoning.description: The model's own thinking channel (``message.reasoning`` on the OpenAI-compat wire); empty for non-reasoning models. A CORE field: a model with nowhere to put its internal process answers without one, so the slot is part of the ask and capturing it is part of the contract. Strictly ANALYTICAL — it rides the ledger to the audit trail and the operator's node detail, and must NEVER feed a gate, metric, validator, scorer, or cache key. Having no code reader is by design; do not delete it as dead surface.
reasoning.title: Reasoning

schema_repair_errors.description: The schema rules each retried attempt broke, one entry per paid retry before the parsed response landed — empty on a clean first parse. Its length is the retry count: bad templates produce schema-noncompliant JSON and silently double-up the LLM spend, and the entries say which rule the prompt fails to teach.
schema_repair_errors.title: Schema Repair Errors

served_by.description: WHICH upstream host answered, where the provider is a gateway that routes onward; ``None`` where it is its own host. Distinct from the provider, which names who we called and so reads the same for every route through it. Analytical like ``reasoning`` — never a gate, metric or cache key.
served_by.title: Served By

tool_calls.description: The calls the model asked for, in its order; empty where it answered in text or was offered no tools. A tool call's ``content`` may be empty: the calls are the answer.
tool_calls.title: Tool Calls

usage.description: What this call consumed. A provider's own spelling stops at the client that parses it: every client normalizes to this account, and no consumer converts.

ManifestSwitch.description: A switch: the whole manifest ``extends`` names, each node ``swap`` names replaced by another manifest's node of its type.
ManifestSwitch.title: ManifestSwitch

NodeKind.description: Closed: an unlisted ``type:`` is refused at parse. A GATEWAY runs another pipeline and owns no config.
NodeKind.title: NodeKind

OptimizerPromptTemplate.title: OptimizerPromptTemplate

PipelineManifest.description: A `pipeline.yaml` typed at load — an optimizer's, or the bench's check-in.
PipelineManifest.title: PipelineManifest

shape.description:
What a fetch of a route's hosts answered, and when: no ceiling where no host prices it. It
names its route and hosts, which the one refresher reads back (`refresh_route_answers`), and
*since*, its route's first answer of that fate, which a re-fetch answering the same keeps.
shape.title: RouteAnswer

SourceFacts.description: A function of ONE source text: ``source_scan.py`` resolves another module's imports.
SourceFacts.title: SourceFacts

SourceReads.description: A whole module's own names are left out: they are hashed with it.
SourceReads.title: SourceReads

ConsentRecord.description: ``accepted_at`` is SERVER-stamped, never client-supplied: its legal weight rests on that clock.
ConsentRecord.title: ConsentRecord

demo_mode_enabled.description: Surface the built-in try-and-learn demo dataset in the collection. On by default for new users; the account toggles it in its preferences.
demo_mode_enabled.title: Demo Mode Enabled

terms_accepted.description: Provable Terms-acceptance record (version + server-stamped timestamp) per acting principal: the account's own and each delegate's. Absent until it clears the consent gate.
terms_accepted.title: Terms Accepted
